title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in 'Variations sur l'équation des lacets', Grothendieck studies the profinite Grothendieck–Teichmüller group (written 𝔊⁺ / 𝔊^♮ here; the next page names them \widehat{GT}^+ and \widehat{GT}^♮) through auxiliary groups indexed by a pair (ρ,σ). The pair is probably a pair of torsion/'dihedral' data; the previous page mentions 'l'imaginaire diédral', so this may concern the action of GT-type groups twisted by finite symmetry data. This page is item 5° of a list of auxiliary groups announced on p. 639. It defines S_0M_{ρ,σ}, M_{ρ,σ}^♮, S_0Γ_{ρ,σ}, Γ_{ρ,σ} 'as on p. 583'.

The pattern is a fibre product over a common finite quotient γ = γ_{ρ,σ}:
- (77): S_0M = Z ×_γ N_ρ ×_γ N_σ ×_γ G. Here Z = Z_{ρ,σ} is probably a centralizer-type group, N_ρ, N_σ normalizer-type groups, and G = G_{ρ,σ} a GT-type group, each with a surjection onto γ. The ♮ variant replaces G by G^♮ (and, per the next page, Z by \bar Z).
- First (78)/(79): S_0Γ = Z ×_γ N_ρ ×_γ N_σ and Γ = N_ρ ×_γ N_σ.
- Second (78): M ≃ N_ρ ×_γ N_σ ×_γ G and M^♮ ≃ N_ρ ×_γ N_σ ×_γ G^♮. The '×' written here must be read as ×_γ.

Forgetting the G-factor gives surjections M → Γ and S_0M → S_0Γ with kernel ker(G→γ) = 𝔊⁺ (resp. 𝔊^♮). Forgetting the Z-factor gives S_0(·) → (·). Inclusions G^♮ ⊂ G give ♮ → plain maps. This yields the cube (79) of short exact sequences 1 → 𝔊 → (S_0)M → (S_0)Γ → 1.

Writing SX := ker(X → γ), each fibre product over γ is an extension of γ by the product of the kernels. This gives (80)–(84):
- 1 → L_0 × SN_ρ × SN_σ × 𝔊 → S_0M → γ → 1, with L_0 = SZ;
- 1 → SN_ρ × SN_σ × 𝔊 → M → γ → 1;
- 1 → L_0 × SN_ρ × SN_σ → S_0Γ → γ → 1;
- 1 → SN_ρ × SN_σ → Γ → γ → 1.

The next page adds the compatibilities S_0M ≃ M ×_Γ S_0Γ. It also gives GT⁺/GT^♮ ≅ G/G^♮ ≅ M/M^♮, which follows since all are kernels over the same γ.

The purpose is bookkeeping: to see the actions of the ♮-groups G^♮, M^♮ as induced from larger 'fourre-tout' groups (next page). Grothendieck himself doubts the S_0 variants are useful.
errors: Equation numbering is muddled: (7[8]9) was corrected to (78) while a second block is also labelled (78), (79) is reused for the diagram, and (82) is skipped.

In (78) and in the second line of (78)/(79) the products are written as plain ×, but they must be fibre products over γ_{ρ,σ} for the exact sequences (81), (84) to hold. In the S_0Γ formula the second × is likewise unsubscripted.

L_0 and L_0^♮ are both labelled SZ_{ρ,σ}, but the next page uses \bar Z_{ρ,σ} for the ♮ variant, so the ♮ kernel should be S\bar Z. S_0Γ^♮ appears in the diagram and in (83) but is only defined implicitly.

In the diagram the row through S_0Γ^♮ lacks the terminal →1. Γ and Γ^♮ appear to coincide, since both use N^♮, so the vertical arrow between them is presumably an identity. These are minor and do not affect correctness.

ideas.what: Auxiliary groups for studying the profinite Grothendieck–Teichmüller group: fibre products over a finite quotient γ_{ρ,σ} of normalizer/centralizer-type groups and GT-type groups, together with the resulting cube of extensions.
ideas.modern_name: Fibre-product (pullback) extensions of a finite group; GT-type subgroups and their variants (GT⁺, GT^♮)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Profinite GT is credited to Drinfeld (1990) and Ihara; the program to Grothendieck's Esquisse (1984). The fibre-product bookkeeping is standard group theory.
ideas.where_published: Unpublished archive notes (cote 140-3); GT itself is foreshadowed in Esquisse d'un programme.

ideas.what: Comparison isomorphism GT⁺/GT^♮ ≅ G_{ρ,σ}/G^♮_{ρ,σ} ≅ M_{ρ,σ}/M^♮_{ρ,σ} (announced on the next page), implied by the cube on this page.
ideas.modern_name: Isomorphism of quotients in a pullback square of extensions

missed.claim: The 'dihedral imaginary' investigation (previous page) is explicitly abandoned. The S_0-variants are introduced with doubt about their usefulness, so the thread of using (ρ,σ)-indexed auxiliary groups to realise actions of GT^♮ as induced actions is left incomplete. The page itself contains only formal bookkeeping, with no new result.
missed.quote: Je ne suis pas sûr que les variantes So (So M, So M^♮, So Γ) soient très utiles.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only as a historical document of Grothendieck's own GT-variants (GT⁺ vs GT^♮) predating or parallel to Drinfeld/Ihara. Mathematically the content on this page is routine.

deep.surprise_reason: Purely formal group-theoretic bookkeeping: fibre products over a finite quotient and the resulting short exact sequences. It is correct up to notational slips and of interest only as part of the larger unpublished GT-related manuscript.
transcription_corrections: The '(7[-8-]9)' label appears to be a (79) corrected to (78); there are effectively two blocks labelled (78), joined by a bracket in the margin.
In (77), first line, the first fibre product is ×_{γ_{ρ,σ}} and the N's carry an overwritten/struck decoration (♮ crossed out or replaced), consistent with the transcription.
The kernels in the diagram are gothic 𝔊⁺ and 𝔊^♮; the second line of (81) has 𝔊 (probably 𝔊⁺).
In (84) the struck-out first factor appears to be L_0 (or Z), heavily crossed out, leaving SN_ρ^♮ × SN_σ^♮.
